title: Student questions: email is the record
summary: What you settle on the spot, what goes to email, and the words to use.

la: Settle quick questions on the spot
Send everything else to the Lab email
Answer routine Lab emails from the templates
lc: Answer emails the lab assistants forward

sections.title: Why email
sections.text: Email gives every request a date, a sender and a written answer that anyone on staff can find later. A spoken promise at the desk disappears when your shift ends. So the rule is simple: if you can't settle it right there, the student puts it in an email to {email}.

sections.title: Student privacy (FERPA)
list: Talk about a student's grades, scores, placement or records only with that student, by email from their UNG address.
Not at the desk or on the phone, and never with parents, friends or classmates. Don't confirm whether someone is in a class.
Email from a personal address: ask them to write from their UNG email. See [Email replies](#/replies/ungmail).
Student names, grades, videos and files stay in D2L, Bongo and the Lab email. Never in texts, personal email, your own drive, a converter website or an AI tool.
Log out of shared Lab computers and close the inbox when you step away.
sections.note: Lab staff complete FERPA training. Not sure if you can share something? Don't. Send it to email.

sections.title: Settle on the spot
list: Checking out or returning an iPad or accessories
Finding a seat or a working station
Mango sign-up on a campus computer
Bongo and browser fixes from the Bongo tutorial
Lab hours and whether the Lab is open now
sections.note: Not sure of the exact answer? Don't guess. Send it to email.

sections.title: Always send to email
list: Grades, scores or a grade someone else gave
Late labs, missed labs and excused absences
Complaints about a class, a lab assistant or a grade
Accommodations (the coordinator handles these with SAS)

sections.title: What to say
sections.script: I want to make sure this gets to the right person and stays on record. Please email {email} with your full name, your class (for example, SPAN 1001, section 02) and your question. We'll answer you by email.
sections.note: On the phone, say the same thing. Don't take messages on paper and don't promise an answer.

sections.title: The Lab inbox
steps: Routine question (hours, setup, how-to): reply from the [Email replies](#/replies).
Anything on the always-send list: forward it to the coordinator with one line on what the student needs.
Leave the email in the inbox so the record stays complete.

sections.title: Coordinator
list: Answer forwarded emails, or forward to the department with the student's details
